official_page_title: Post-wildfire Flood and Debris Flow: 2014 Silverado Fire
official_page_event_statement: The USGS page states that an automated rain-triggered camera at the outlet of a 0.6 km^2 basin within the Silverado Fire burn area recorded the initial surge and peak flow triggered by a storm on 2015-07-19; the peak occurred about three minutes after the initial surge.
fire_reference: 2014 Silverado Fire (burn area); event date comes from the official page description, not the fire year in the title.
location: Silverado Fire burn area, Orange County, California; outlet of a small basin (USGS page states 0.6 km^2). Exact camera coordinates are not given on the source page.
video_sample_timing: stts contains one run: 3917 samples, each 1000 ticks at timebase 1/30000 s (30 fps); no ctts composition-offset table. FFmpeg showinfo confirmed selected decoded source-frame PTS values below.

content_review.review_scope: Sparse direct frame extraction at 0, 1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 26, 52, 65, 78, 104, 125, and 130.533 s; not a full-video review or full decode.
content_review.viewpoint: The same channel scene is visible across sampled frames, but the four interior frames show measurable image-plane shifts in matched static-looking vegetation/rock features. Viewpoint/framing stability is therefore pending; sampled frames do not justify claiming a continuously fixed framing or single uninterrupted camera view.
content_review.opening_and_overlays: Black at PTS 0; sampled PTS 1, 3, and 5 show a USGS logo card. The channel view is present by 10 s. A persistent USGS watermark appears on scene frames. No sampled frame showed a debris-flow class caption or date overlay.
content_review.visual_content: Sparse sampled frames show a muddy/turbid, flow-like visual appearance in the channel and different image content at the sampled times. These still samples do not establish flow speed, continuous motion, or temporal continuity. Event-level relevance is supported by the official source description; framewise labels and interval boundaries remain unreviewed.
content_review.remaining_review: Review the complete clip for camera movement, digital reframing, edits, and any ordinary flood/water-only phases; the four-frame local feature comparison cannot distinguish camera/crop motion from local vegetation movement or establish continuity.

media_verification_scope: Original MP4 downloaded directly from the USGS-linked S3 asset. MP4 track/sample tables parsed; selected frames at known source PTS decoded locally with FFmpeg 4.2.2 without reported errors. Whole-file decode and end-to-end decode-error count were not run.
sampling_input_compatibility: The 30 fps video-track rate and the 13 sampled PTS values describe the published MP4 encoding timeline only. They do not establish the source camera acquisition rate, independent real-world observations, or that 16 independent observations exist in any real 3-second window. Actual capture cadence and compatibility with the protocol remain unverified.
independence_status: New nominal event and new region/site compared with listed current catalog entries; exact source identity, event independence, and development-pool overlap remain pending.
dataset_status: candidate; unassigned; not frozen; no model scoring

viewpoint_stability_check.scope: Four exact source-PTS frames at 26, 52, 78, and 104 seconds; no additional video download or full decode.
viewpoint_stability_check.conclusion: Local scale estimates near 1.0 provide no evidence of a major zoom change in this ROI; limited sparse sampling cannot exclude digital reframing or camera movement elsewhere. The measured image shifts mean viewpoint stability remains pending.

frame_extraction_record.output_log_note: The FFmpeg combined stdout/stderr was returned in the interactive command output and was not persisted to a file. No historical log is recreated.
